note: Read in full 2026-09-17 (action=raw, HTTP 200). Two things here bear on the scene date. First, THE DISTRICT'S OWN CONSTRUCTION SPAN, printed in the infobox as 'built 1836-1892' - the Henry B. Clarke House of 1836 at the near end and the 1890s houses at the far end. A representative date for the district's mature state has to sit inside that span and after the buildings that give the district its character, which puts it in the second half of it. Second, the district's EXTENT, which is what the successor terrain and street tickets have to cover: the 1800 and 1900 blocks of South Prairie, the 1800 block of South Indiana, and 211-217 East Cullerton. The page also records that this ground was the site of the 1812 Battle of Fort Dearborn, which is the same ground T-0468 to T-0472 model at their own epoch - the two South Through Time scenes share a location and not a surface, and that is exactly why they need separate terrain epochs. Its Glessner dates disagree with the Glessner article's and with themselves; see wikipedia_glessner_house, which holds the full spread. Graded asset_use=orientation: it is good for which blocks and roughly what period, and it is not a source anything may be traced from.
